new_bank_questions.title: Uncertainty beyond a conditional shrinkage rule
new_bank_questions.body: A hierarchical analysis assigns equal posterior probability to two hyperparameter regimes. In regime A a group effect has conditional posterior N(5,1), and in regime B it has conditional posterior N(9,1). Find the marginal posterior mean and variance of the group effect. What variance term would a calculation based on only one regime omit?
new_bank_questions.answer: The marginal mean is (5+9)/2=7. The law of total variance gives E[Var(theta|regime,y)]+Var(E[theta|regime,y])=1+[(5−7)^2+(9−7)^2]/2=1+4=5. Fixing a single regime would retain only conditional variance 1 and omit the between-regime variance 4. This is the distinction between a conditional shrinkage calculation and full averaging over uncertain hyperparameters.
